housing.text: Archuleta twice voted for SB 9, which required approval of qualifying two-unit developments and urban lot splits.
housing.quote: Archuleta, Atkins, Becker, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dahle, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Gonzalez, Grove, Hertzberg, Hueso

safety.text: While promoting legislation increasing penalties for repeat theft, Archuleta said law enforcement should have every available tool to keep communities safe.
safety.quote: We must take steps to ensure that law enforcement has every tool available to them to keep our communities safe

sentencing.text: Archuleta introduced SB 923 to impose jail or prison terms on people convicted of a third theft offense.
sentencing.quote: The bill ensures that, beginning on a third offense, serial thieves are charged with between 6 months and three years’ imprisonment.

immigration.text: Archuleta voted for AB 1766, which made state identification cards available regardless of immigration status.
immigration.quote: Allen, Archuleta, Atkins, Becker, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Glazer, Gonzalez, Hertzberg, Hueso

guns.text: Archuleta twice voted for SB 2, which tightened concealed-carry licensing and restricted firearms in specified sensitive places.
guns.quote: Allen, Archuleta, Ashby, Atkins, Becker, Blakespear, Bradford, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Glazer, Gonzalez, Laird

cannabis.text: Archuleta voted in committee and on the Senate floor for AB 1775, which expanded regulated cannabis-consumption businesses by permitting food and beverage sales.
cannabis.quote: Allen, Alvarado-Gil, Archuleta, Atkins, Becker, Blakespear, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dahle, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Glazer

energy.text: Archuleta twice voted for SB 1020, which established interim clean-electricity targets and a 100-percent clean-power goal.
energy.quote: Allen, Archuleta, Atkins, Becker, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Glazer, Gonzalez, Hertzberg, Hueso

voting.text: Archuleta voted for AB 37, which permanently required mailing a ballot to every active registered voter.
voting.quote: Allen, Archuleta, Atkins, Becker, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Glazer, Gonzalez, Hertzberg, Hueso

tax.text: Martinez says she would cut taxes and oppose tax increases affecting small businesses and independent workers.
tax.quote: I will fight to lower the cost of living by cutting unnecessary taxes, reducing regulatory burdens, and making it easier to build and grow.

housing.text: Martinez supports fast-tracking housing construction by reducing reviews and litigation-related delays.
housing.quote: Housing: Make it easier to build affordable single-family home communities for teachers, first responders, and young families, while fast-tracking housing construction by cutting burdensome reviews and stopping lawsuit abuse that delays projects and drives up costs.

safety.text: Martinez says she would support law enforcement and hold repeat offenders accountable.
safety.quote: I will support law enforcement, hold repeat offenders accountable, and push back on policies that have made our communities less safe.

energy.text: Martinez supports expanding energy production and reversing policies she says increase utility costs.
energy.quote: Utilities: Bring down the cost of electricity and basic utilities by expanding reliable energy production, modernizing infrastructure, and stopping costly state policies that keep driving rates higher.
